content.text:
Compiles and behaves identically. Here's what changed:

**`Preprocessor<T>.andThen`** (new default method):
```java
default Preprocessor<T> andThen(Preprocessor<T> next) {
    return input -> next.process(this.process(input));
}
```
Returns a new `Preprocessor<T>` lambda that pipes `this.process` into `next.process`. Because it's a default method on the interface, every implementor gets composition for free — no base class or utility wrapper needed. Chains of arbitrary length work by calling `.andThen` repeatedly; each call produces another `Preprocessor<T>`.

**`MinLengthPreprocessor`** (new concrete class): validates the array has at least `minLength` elements before the two-pointer algorithm runs. It's the natural second step after `SortedArrayPreprocessor` has verified ordering — the algorithm needs at least 2 elements to form a pair.

**`main`**: builds the pipeline explicitly before passing it to `TwoPointers`:
```java
Data.Preprocessor<int[]> preprocessor = new Data.SortedArrayPreprocessor()
    .andThen(new Data.MinLengthPreprocessor(2));
```
`TwoPointers` itself is unchanged — it still takes a single `Preprocessor<int[]>`, oblivious to whether it's a single step or a composed chain.
